paper_metadata.title: Confidence Estimation for Knowledge Base Population
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of Recent Advances in Natural Language Processing (RANLP 2013)
paper_metadata.abstract: Information extraction systems automatically extract structured information from machine-readable documents, such as newswire, web, and multimedia. Despite significant improvement, the performance is far from perfect. Hence, it is useful to accurately estimate confidence in the correctness of the extracted information. Using the Knowledge Base Population Slot Filling task as a case study, we propose a confidence estimation model based on the Maximum Entropy framework, obtaining an average precision of 83.5%, Pearson coefficient of 54.2%, and 2.3% absolute improvement in F-measure score through a weighted voting strategy.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses unreliable intermediate outputs from multi-pipeline Knowledge Base Population (KBP) slot filling. It estimates each extracted slot fill's probability of correctness so heterogeneous pipeline outputs can be comparably re-ranked, filtered, and aggregated into more accurate KB population results.

methodology.description: Execution order: (1) retrieve documents matching a person or organization query name, optionally using query expansion; (2) preprocess retrieved text with POS tagging, name tagging, and coreference resolution; (3) run six parallel slot-filling pipelines—two hand-coded-pattern systems, two semi-automatically bootstrapped pattern systems, one name-coreference system, and one distant-supervision system—to produce intermediate query-slot-response fills; (4) compute a MaxEnt correctness probability for every intermediate response from response, pipeline, local-sentence, and global corpus features; (5) remove low-confidence responses and perform weighted response voting, summing supporting probabilities for each response entity; (6) select the highest-weight response for single-valued slots and all non-redundant fills for list-valued slots, then optionally suppress final fills below a final-confidence threshold. The confidence layer is trained/evaluated using ten-fold cross-validation over prior TAC KBP slot-filling evaluation data.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The task supplies a predefined KBP slot schema: 42 slots (26 person and 16 organization), with single-valued and list-valued constraints. The method populates these predefined attributes rather than discovering an ontology or schema.

input_output.input_type: Newswire and web-document corpus, plus person and organization entity queries and an initial KB derived from Wikipedia infoboxes.
input_output.input_granularity: Corpus documents are retrieved per person/organization query; answer-extraction evidence is a supporting sentence containing the query and response, with document-level global co-occurrence features.
input_output.output_representation: Slot-fill response tuples <Query ID, Slot Name, Response Fill>, each accompanied by a supporting document ID; final output is one best fill for a single-valued slot or a non-redundant list of fills for a list-valued slot, with confidence scores.

models_and_tools: Six parallel KBP slot-filling pipelines: two hand-coded-pattern, two bootstrapped-pattern, one name-coreference, and one distant-supervision pipeline
Document retrieval with query-name match or query expansion
POS tagging, name tagging, and coreference resolution
Shortest dependency-path, named-entity-margin, POS trigram, corpus co-occurrence, conditional-probability, and PMI features
datasets: Merged TAC KBP Slot Filling evaluation data from 2010, 2011, and 2012: 280 total queries and 31,878 intermediate responses
TAC KBP 2012 source corpus: 3.7 million newswire articles and web texts; initial KB derived from Wikipedia infoboxes

metrics: Average precision of confidence-ranked intermediate responses
Pearson's r correlation between confidence and binary correctness
Wilcoxon Matched-Pairs Signed-Ranks Significance Test (99.8% confidence for F-measure gain)
baselines: Basic plurality-voting response-combination system, in which each intermediate response contributes equally
Random confidence values sampled uniformly from 0 to 1
Worst-case confidence ranking that places incorrect responses above correct responses
evaluation.setting: Ten-fold cross-validation on merged KBP 2010–2012 data. Each fold contains 14 person and 14 organization queries and their intermediate responses; the MaxEnt model trains on nine folds and scores the remaining fold. Voting comparison uses τ=0 and η=0.17, with response correctness judged by answer string while ignoring document ID. Confidence-ranking evaluation uses all intermediate responses.

value: The MaxEnt confidence estimator achieved average precision 0.835 and Pearson's r 0.542 when ranking intermediate slot-filling responses; random confidence gave average precision 0.525 and r=0.001, while the worst-case ranking had average precision 0.330.
Confidence-weighted voting improved final slot-filling F-measure from 0.289 to 0.312 (+0.023 absolute) and precision from 0.351 to 0.441 (+0.090), while recall decreased from 0.246 to 0.241 (-0.005).
Raising the intermediate-response threshold increased precision toward about 1 while recall declined toward 0; confidence intervals with higher scores consistently had greater final-fill precision.

Among separately applied features, slot-response length and response-document count were the best correctness predictors; dependency-path length was also significant, whereas NE margin contributed minimally.

value: Author/experimental result: The method produces confidence scores that correlate substantially with response correctness (average precision 0.835; Pearson's r 0.542), enabling useful ranking of intermediate slot fills.

Author/experimental result: Integrating those scores into weighted voting improves the evaluated KBP slot-filling F-measure by 2.3 absolute points and precision by 9.0 points, with only a 0.5-point recall loss.

Review-level inference: The method is practical for heterogeneous legacy extraction pipelines because it uses pipeline-agnostic response, context, corpus, and prior-pipeline-performance features to calibrate and aggregate their outputs rather than replacing the extractors.

value: Review-level inference: The contribution of weighted voting is only evaluated over the authors' own six-pipeline slot-filling system and merged historical KBP evaluation data; the paper does not provide evidence that the confidence model transfers to other extraction architectures, domains, or schemas.

Review-level inference: The final scoring comparison ignores supporting-document ID, so it does not measure whether the confidence layer improves provenance correctness required by the original KBP task.

Review-level inference: Precision rises by filtering as the confidence threshold increases, but recall falls toward zero; threshold selection therefore remains an application-dependent precision–recall trade-off.

Review-level inference: Robust confidence calibration for extraction outputs from new pipelines, domains, and schemas remains unresolved by this single-system, cross-validation evaluation.

Review-level inference: How to jointly optimize confidence thresholds for both answer quality and provenance correctness remains unresolved; the paper reports an answer-string evaluation and a threshold-driven precision–recall trade-off.
